title: LP2-31: periodic IoC with within-row shuffles
question: Does the largest pooled column IoC over periods 2–20 exceed shuffles that preserve every archived row’s rune multiset?
summary: The observed period-13 peak is unchanged. With within-row shuffling, 245 of 999 null maxima meet or exceed it; corrected Monte Carlo p = 0.246.

scope.representation: 269 archived runes; headings included; non-alphabet characters removed; no corrections.
scope.procedure: Keep the twelve archived transcription row boundaries fixed; shuffle each row independently while preserving its rune counts; concatenate in original row order. Pool residue-column pairs over the whole stream, maximize over periods, and compare against identically scanned within-row shuffles.
scope.parameters: Periods 2-20 inclusive; offset zero; 999 trials; seed 330131; >= ties; plus-one Monte Carlo correction; alpha 0.05.
scope.exclusions: Other pages, periods outside 2-20, regional variants, corrected streams, word/punctuation-preserving nulls, decryption and key searches.

finding: Same observed maximum: period 13, 216/5300. Within-row null: 245 of 999 maxima at least as large; corrected p=0.246, above 0.05. Whole-page baseline p=0.214.
limitations: A follow-up chosen after seeing the baseline, not independent confirmation. Row-conditioned exchangeability still does not preserve words or local order. Neither result proves randomness or rules out a cipher. No adjustment for comparing null models. Human review pending.
next_steps: Human review of the row-conditioned null and boundaries. Any changed page, regions, statistic or period range needs a declared variant.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.10 standard library. Separate check: python experiments/records/lp2-31-row-shuffle-ioc/check.py

review.reviewer: Codex — full rerun and pair-count checks; human review pending
